To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) net liver weights are a function of the body size and age in the rabbit, (2) net liver weights vary widely within an age group, and (3) net liver weight has no effect on the plasma membrane function of the liver in the rabbit.
the net liver weight of the rabbit can be established by the isotopic measurement of residual blood in a liver sample and that this value is a linear function of body weight.
the liver weight of the New Zealand White rabbit is proportional to the body weight and that the maximal hepatic uptake of asialoglycoproteins is independent of the liver weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the net weight of the organ and its relevance to hepatic clearance function, a subject which has been neglected to date.
the relationship between the size of the rabbit liver, its composition, and its ability to clear a plasma protein from the blood.
the relationship between liver size and the capacity for asialoglycoside uptake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the net weight of the hepatic tissue is not a limiting factor in the asialoglycoproteins clearance.
the net weight of the hepatic parenchyma is the only parameter of importance for asialoglyco-protein clearance.
the net weight of the normal liver is not a critical factor in determining the rate of hepatic clearance of asialoglycoproteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the liver is an important organ for clearance of glycoproteins with terminal galactose residues, that the net liver weight is a linear function of body weight in young adult rabbits, and that the plasma membrane function is not affected by storage-related variations in liver size.
the net liver weight of the rabbit is a function of the age and body weight of the animal.
the hepatic function of the rabbit is a function of the net weight of the organ and that this function is independent of the liver size within a wide range of body weights.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver weight of the rabbit is not a constant value.
net liver weight can be estimated with reasonable precision from body weight and age.

the net weight of rabbit livers is proportional to the body weight of the animal and that the plasma clearance of a glycoconjugate is not influenced by changes in the size of the hepatic vascular space.
